source: Minchat Shai on Gen 39:1 quoting the Ramah (the Masorah's two-word list)
claim_en: Potiphar is ONE written word, full yod and full vav — the Ramah's proof by omission: the Masorah's list of names written TWO words and read one (Poti-fera, Malki-tzedek, Baal-chanan, Tzafnat-paneach) does not count Potiphar. Both Torah stations single-token (39:1 checked bare; 37:36 with its lamed asserted).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 39:20 (the Great Masorah's alphabet-list)
claim_en: asure ha-melekh ('the king's prisoners'): written with VAV, read with YOD — 'the FIRST of the Great Masorah's alphabet of words written vav in the middle and read yod.' SNAPSHOT carries the two-token pair in-stream (bare written form checked, pointed read-form asserted beside it). The Kitzur counts the years in it: ten for the slander of ten brothers, two more for the two remember-me's.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 39:22 (the Ramah; the Meiri; the Hilleli; against the printer)
claim_en: ha-asirim ('ALL the prisoners'): the printer muddled it into the vav-list and Minchat Kohen followed; MS rules with the Ramah, the Meiri, and the Hilleli's note — written with yod after the samekh, lean in the second yod, no written/read pair here, marked UNIQUE. SNAPSHOT writes exactly that, once in the Torah.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 39:8 quoting Rabbeinu Bachya
claim_en: va-yemaen ('and he REFUSED') carries the chain-accent (shalshelet) — Bachya's principle stated on this very word: 'from the accents of the Torah we understand what is not written, as from a man's gestures we know his heart' — the mark draws the refusal out to its utmost. One of the whole-Torah FOUR chain-accent stations (gen_35's census); in-stream.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: 'And all he had he gave into his hand' — the five words' FINAL letters spell leshono ('his TONGUE'): Gabriel came and taught him seventy tongues, and so he prospered. Ordered finals checked in-stream.
middah: E30 (notarikon — the initials, finals, or rearranged letters of the verse's own words, the Kitzur's reading)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 39:20 (the Masorah)
claim_en: asurim ('bound') — the Kitzur's three: two with Joseph and one 'the LORD releases the bound' (Ps 146:7, outside the instrument). The Torah census is exactly the Joseph pair: his own binding (39:20) and his fellow-prisoners' (40:5, next unit's span) — the Kitzur's dialogue rides it: she said 'I will bind you'; he answered 'the LORD releases the bound.'
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 39:15 (the Masorah)
claim_en: harimoti ('I RAISED') — exactly TWICE in the Torah, both Torah-side: Abram's raised hand (the oath refusing Sodom's spoil, 14:22) and the wife's raised voice (the false cry, 39:15): the same word lifts an oath and a lie.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 39:1 (the Masorah)
claim_en: hurad ('Joseph was BROUGHT DOWN') — the Kitzur pairs it with 'brought down to Sheol' (Isaiah, outside the instrument): exile weighed as the grave. The skeleton's own Torah pair: here passive, and re-pointed imperative at 'take DOWN your ornaments' (Exod 33:5, after the calf) — two descents, the slave's and the nation's.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 39:1 (the Masorah)
claim_en: horiduhu ('they brought HIM down' / 'bring HIM down') — exactly TWICE in the Torah: the Ishmaelites bringing Joseph down to Egypt (39:1), and Joseph's own 'bring him down to me' over Benjamin (44:21): because Judah caused the one descent, he must perform the other — the Kitzur's measure-for-measure, census exact.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the bring-him-down word at two seats; measure for measure, E27, the reading)

claim_en: The chapter's pointing set: ka-harimi ('as I raised my voice') — 'the he with sheva-and-patach' (the compound half-vowel), CHECKED under the guttural; le-tzacheq ('to mock me', 39:17) with the chet in segol, and ha-ze ('this') with the zayin dagesheed (asserted).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: roe et-kal ('saw not ANY thing'): MS rules et 'with maqqef and WITHOUT a stress-stroke' in the precise books. SNAPSHOT joins the maqqef (checked) but WRITES the meteg MS's books omit (asserted at build) — a pointing DISCREPANCY, the stream against MS's camp, filed to the watchlist.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 39:7 (Rambam; the Hilleli; the Meiri; Et Sofer)
claim_en: 'And it was after these things' (the wife's eyes lift): the Sephardic precise books write NO paragraph break here; Rambam's list and the Hilleli make it OPEN; the Meiri declines to rule and leaves a closed-parasha gap; Et Sofer holds no-break as the essence. Paragraph layer uninstrumented — filed with the camps recorded.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)
plain (the errand read three ways; the father's image at witness tier; the translation's vote)
claim_en: THE EMPTY HOUSE AND THE FATHER'S IMAGE: 'he came into the house to do his work' is read three ways in the chain — his actual accounts, an INDEED (he came for her), and 'no man of the household there' because all had gone to the Nile festival or the theatre. The received translation votes for the first, rendering the errand as checking the account-books, and the reading adds the restraint's mechanism: he saw his father's image and his blood cooled, the bow drawn and slackened. Dual-track: the machine carries the errand from the grammar and the image at witness tier.

middah: plain (the master's anger aimed at the story; the imprisonment verb as appointment; witness tier)
claim_en: POTIPHAR'S OWN VERDICT: the reading takes the master's anger as directed not at Joseph but at the story — 'I know you did not do it' — and reads the imprisonment verb as an APPOINTMENT rather than a committal, which is why the prison-keeper immediately hands him the house. The machine records the custody with the master's disbelief carried beside it, at witness tier.

THE ACCOMPANIMENT FORMULA FRAMES THE CHAPTER AT FOUR SEATS: 'the LORD was with Joseph' stands at 39:2 and 39:3 in the master's house and again at 39:21 and 39:23 in the prison — two before the fall and two after, an exact frame. The received translation renders each with its Word-as-support formula, the same idiom it uses of Jacob at 48:21 and of Joseph's blessing at 49:25, so the accompaniment is stated in one consistent vocabulary across the whole cycle.
